data.body:
Implemented and pushed for review as Gerrit change 1927 (https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/1927).

Two skill files changed, no code:

**rebar-debug — defect attribution.** Added a required attribution step to Phase 1's exit gate (Stage 3), immediately before the RCA writeback: blame the exact implicated lines, walk through carrier commits, check whether the fix site is even the cause site, recover the ticket from the introducing commit's trailer, record it with --caused-by on the close, and note any divergence from what a mechanical blame would say. Four resolutions enumerated: regression, unmet obligation (missed consumer update), omission by scope-of-work, and unattributable (record the searches, leave the link unset).

The design point that drove most of the text: the blame fallback only looks at paths the FIX touched, so it structurally cannot see the unmet-obligation case where a producer change creates a requirement and a consumer is never updated. The fix lands in consumer code whose lines are old and were correct when written, and blame charges the defect to the consumer's old ticket instead of to the change that shipped the obligation. The skill now carries a date test for detecting this cheaply (implicated lines predating the good-to-bad transition cannot have caused it) and producer-side history search as the recovery.

Also stated that --caused-by is required on the close even when the link was already recorded via rebar link — plan review caught that _apply_caused_by (transition_close.py:198-201) calls derive_caused_by unconditionally when the flag is empty and never checks for an existing edge, so a bare close would add a second, guessed edge beside the proven one.

Close gated on attribution in Reporting back; Defect origin line added to the report-back; link added to the pre-approved own-tracker carve-out; fast-path and Stage 1 hooks wired.

**rebar-debug + rebar-implement — worktree bootstrap.** Both now bootstrap with make worktree name=<branch> (which provisions the venv; a bare git worktree add does not) and carry one pointer to run every command with the worktree venv first on PATH, pointing at docs/local-dev-env.md. This was hit live while doing this work: the fresh worktree had no venv and the pre-commit hook would have failed on missing ruff/mypy.

Gates: plan review PASS (signed at 6a4fd2fb); make lint clean; skill frontmatter gate PASS; test_skill_shared_sync.py 5 passed (shared test-design.md copies untouched).
